note: Standing owner rules from reviews. Every agent reads these (decisions.design_rules) before writing or designing. Add new ones with: python run_agent.py add-rule --rule "..."

rules.rule: An approved design is a quality bar, never a template: every post is a completely new design, not the same layout with new text.
We make real-estate content that preserves the real building; the building's architecture must never change.
The building is the hero: headline and text go in the sky above it or in the foreground below it, never over the building, and no dark gradient may cover the facade.
Do not repeat the same elements between posts (same fact boxes, same split gold/navy call-to-action bar); give each post its own call-to-action treatment.
Use a different render each time (21 renders in assets/renders and assets/original) and do not stick to one colour scheme; vary palette and fonts per post.
For a brand announcement the brand comes first: its logo or name leads, then 'is coming to Shrih Plaza' (e.g. Domino's first, then 'is coming to', then Shrih Plaza).

Use the official Shrih Plaza logo, assets/original/logo-official.png (olive-gold gradient Shri + Plaza lockup with the two hanging lines, source D:/shrih plaza/Untitled design.png with its white background removed, final choice by the owner 2026-10-01), and only the 12 approved brands; never the older posts' extra brands or old phone numbers. Phone: +91 90564 53575.

Workflow: images are made in Adobe (Generative Expand plus sky/lighting grades on the real renders), laid out in Claude Design, and finished in Adobe Express Pro; posts can also be turned into animated reels.
The Shrih Plaza logo must be prominent, never a small corner mark: the official wide lockup at about 24-37% of the canvas width (roughly 260-400 px on a 1080 px post or reel, 115-175 px tall).

Place brand logos cut out, without their white background box; on dark or brand-coloured backgrounds use a reversed version (white wordmark, e.g. assets/original/brands/dominos-reversed.png) with a soft white edge so the logo reads clearly.

Quality bar (owner was impressed, 2026-10-01): the 'Dusk Issue' magazine-cover carousel, where Adobe cuts out the sky so a giant masthead sits behind the roofline and the building stands in front of the text. Aim for this level of idea and depth on every post, but never reuse it as a template.

Take each post's colour theme from its own image: sample the photo's sky, light and facade colours and build the palette from them (e.g. sapphire sky + sunset gold + sandstone for a golden-hour render). Never lay an unrelated colour (like plum over a golden image) on a photo; it looks odd.
